title: DP III: Knapsack Variants & Subsequence (Depth Pass)
relevance: High — post-ladder CF/AtCoder twists on 0/1, multiple, group, and contribution knapsacks plus subsequence-counting / LCS-with-constraints; this is the Div2 C–D / CM band after CSES coins + AtCoder D/E/F.
company_notes: Promo pricing: pay for k items, get floor(k/m) free → K for the Price of One (ecommerce OA). Team/bug budget: assign lines to n people under a global bug cap → Writing Code (0/1 with two capacities). Nested inventory: each shelf/day local pack, choose under global k → Porcelain / Timetable. String analytics: count abc with wildcards, or LCS that must not contain a banned token → Number of Subsequences / Lucky Common Subsequence.

phases.goal: Confirm the candidate sees the same knapsack/LCS engines under contest wrappers that force a rewrite first.

must_hit.point: Same engines as the base topic—fill a capacity, flip to value-dimension, or align two sequences—but statements force a rewrite first: free-every-k, huge W with few weight classes or n≤40, shelves/days/lessons groups, or subsequence asks with ?, forced length, or a virus string.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names fill-capacity / value-flip / two-sequence engines and lists several rewrite skins (free-every-k, huge W, groups, subsequence constraints).

must_hit.point: Spot it when a classic knapsack/LCS sits under a contest packing: deadlines, nested groups, or contribution over all subsets/segments.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says classic knapsack/LCS under deadlines, nested groups, or contribution-over-subsets/segments.

must_hit.point: OA skins: promo pay-k-get-floor(k/m)-free (K for the Price of One); team lines with bug cap (Writing Code); nested shelf/day packs under global k (Porcelain / Timetable); abc with ? or LCS avoiding a banned token (Number of Subsequences / Lucky Common Subsequence).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those four Where-it-appears skins.

probes: What makes this depth-pass knapsack/subsequence DP rather than a plain Book Shop or LCS template?
If the statement hides free-every-k, nested shelves/days, contribution over subsets, or a virus-constrained LCS, what family do you reach for?

hints.1: Ask whether the template is disguised even though the engine is still fill-capacity, value-flip, or two-sequence DP.
hints.2: Cue: free-every-k; W huge with few classes or n≤40; per-group bests then group knapsack; contribution over subsets/segments; subsequence with ? or forbidden pattern.
hints.3: Say: same engines as base; recognize under deadlines/nested groups/contribution; OA maps are K for the Price of One, Writing Code, Porcelain/Timetable, Number of Subsequences / Lucky Common Subsequence.

phases.goal: Pick the right rewrite—freebie accounting, weight-class/MITM, group best[t], binary multiple, contribution, or constrained subsequence—before coding.

must_hit.point: Free-every-k (K for the Price of One): sort ascending; paying for i items unlocks ⌊i/k⌋ free ones from the most expensive paid; hard version uses prefix sums + DP over how many paid blocks you buy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States sort ascending, freebies from expensive end, and hard-version prefix + paid-block DP.

must_hit.point: Huge W, small structure: few distinct weights → knapsack only on weight classes (e.g. w_i ∈ [w1, w1+3] by count and extra-weight); n≤40 → split, enumerate 2^{n/2} subset sums, binary-search complements.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates weight-class DP from MITM split with sorted subset sums and upper_bound complements.

must_hit.point: Nested / group knapsack (Porcelain, Timetable): for each group compute best[t] = value of taking exactly t items from that group, then 0/1-knapsack the groups into the global budget.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States per-group best[t] then 0/1 over groups into global k/budget.

must_hit.point: Multiple knapsack (Book Shop II): binary-split counts into pseudo-items 1,2,4,…,remain and run ordinary 0/1—do not loop cnt naively. Contribution DP: each subset/segment adds f(sum); push updates that add contribution of newly formed sums (often mod a prime), not one optimum.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names binary grouping into 0/1 pseudo-items and/or contribution push updates instead of a single optimum.

must_hit.point: Subsequence: dp[i][j] consume/skip; with ? multiply three branches; with a forbidden pattern fold a KMP failure link into the LCS state so the virus never completes. Offset/signed knapsack: map difference d to index d+OFFSET.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions consume/skip, ? three branches, LCS+KMP virus state, and/or OFFSET for signed imbalance.

probes: Before coding, is this free-every-k, weight-class/MITM, group best[t], binary multiple, contribution, or constrained subsequence?
For K for the Price of One vs Simple Knapsack / Programming Contest vs Porcelain / Timetable vs Book Shop II vs Lucky Common Subsequence, which rewrite do you pick?

hints.1: Classify freebie rewrite vs huge-W structure vs nested groups vs binary multiples vs contribution vs string automaton.
hints.2: Free-every-k sorts and takes expensive freebies; few weights → class DP; n≤40 → MITM; groups → best[t] then group 0/1; multiples → 1,2,4,…; contribution pushes f(sum); virus LCS folds KMP.
hints.3: Say: sort + ⌊i/k⌋ freebies / prefix block DP; [w1,w1+3] or 2^{n/2} MITM; best[t] then group knapsack; binary-split multiples; contribution not one optimum; ? three branches or LCS+KMP; OFFSET for signed d.

phases.goal: Verify binary grouping, MITM half-sums, group best[t] fills, contribution pushes, OFFSET arrays, bitset shifts, and construction recovery.

must_hit.point: Binary-group multiple copies into 1,2,4,…,remain pseudo-items and run ordinary 0/1; never for _ in cnt inside the capacity loop unless cnt is tiny.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on binary grouping into 0/1 items and rejects naive cnt loops in the capacity pass.

must_hit.point: MITM when n≤40 and capacity/T is huge: split halves, keep sorted vectors of achievable sums per half, upper_bound complements.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes split, sorted half subset sums, and binary-search/upper_bound complements.

must_hit.point: Group/nested: precompute per-group best[t] (e.g. shelf prefix/suffix best for t cups; day best hours saved by skipping t lessons), then 0/1-knapsack groups into global k.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States per-group best[t] then knapsack groups into global budget/k.

must_hit.point: Contribution: update DP by adding f(sum) for newly formed subset/segment sums (All Subsets mod 998244353; All Segments by extending the right endpoint)—not a single optimum pack. Bitset reachability: dp |= dp<<w, then peel forced items or argue unique totals.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions contribution push updates (and/or mod 998244353) and bitset shift reachability.

must_hit.point: Offset arrays for signed imbalance (Coding Company: map d to d+OFFSET). Recover construction when needed (Checkout / Bookshelf): parent pointers or redo DP knowing the optimum budget. Lucky Common Subsequence: LCS state includes automaton position via KMP failure links.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names OFFSET indexing, parent/redo reconstruction, and/or LCS+automaton state.

probes: How do you implement multiple knapsack without a naive cnt loop, and when do you switch to MITM?
Sketch group best[t] → global knapsack, a contribution push update, or bitset dp |= dp<<w.

hints.1: Think binary pseudo-items, half subset sums, per-group best[t], and contribution vs reachability bitsets.
hints.2: Multiples → 1,2,4,… then 0/1; n≤40 → sorted half sums + upper_bound; groups → best[t] then global 0/1; contribution adds f(sum); bitset shifts; OFFSET for signed d; parents for construction.
hints.3: Say: binary-group not cnt loop; MITM sorted halves; Porcelain/Timetable best[t] then knapsack; contribution not one optimum; dp |= dp<<w; d+OFFSET; KMP in LCS state; parents/redo for Checkout/Bookshelf.

phases.goal: State when MITM, weight-class DP, or binary grouping replace a full-capacity knapsack because W or T is huge.

must_hit.point: When n≤40 and capacity/T is huge, MITM: enumerate 2^{n/2} subset sums per half, keep sorted vectors, binary-search complements—do not DP the full capacity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes n≤40, 2^{n/2} half enumeration, and sorted-complement search instead of full-capacity DP.

must_hit.point: When W is 10^9 but weights have small structure (few distinct classes, e.g. w_i ∈ [w1, w1+3]), DP by (count, extra-weight) or weight classes instead of indexing the full W.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites W is 10^9 with few classes / [w1, w1+3] and rejects full-W indexing.

must_hit.point: Multiple knapsack: binary-split counts into 1,2,4,…,remain pseudo-items so the 0/1 pass stays over log-grouped items; naive looping cnt inside capacity is the wrong scaling. Bitset dp |= dp<<w when only reachability or uniqueness of a sum matters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts binary grouping with naive cnt loops, and names bitset reachability when values are not needed.

probes: When do n≤40 / W is 10^9 force MITM or weight-class DP instead of a full-capacity table?
What changes about the knapsack pass when you binary-group multiples or switch to bitset reachability?

hints.1: Separate the n≤40 MITM fit check from few-weight-class and binary-grouping rewrites.
hints.2: n≤40 + huge T → 2^{n/2} sorted halves; W is 10^9 + few classes → (count, extra-weight); multiples → 1,2,4,…; reachability → bitset shifts.
hints.3: Say: MITM when n≤40; class DP when W is 10^9 with [w1, w1+3]-style structure; binary-group multiples; bitset when only yes/no or uniqueness matters.

phases.goal: Catch naive cnt loops, missing freebie/group rewrites, optimizing one pack when contribution is required, and broken ? / virus / OFFSET handling.

must_hit.point: Looping cnt naively inside the capacity loop for multiple knapsack instead of binary-splitting into 1,2,4,…,remain pseudo-items.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects to binary grouping into ordinary 0/1 items unless cnt is tiny.

must_hit.point: Treating free-every-k or nested shelves/days as a plain item knapsack without the rewrite (sort + expensive freebies / paid-block DP; or per-group best[t] then group-knapsack).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on the freebie rewrite or best[t]-then-groups rewrite before the 0/1 pass.

must_hit.point: Computing one optimal pack when the problem is contribution over all subsets/segments (Knapsack for All Subsets / All Segments)—must push f(sum) updates, often mod a prime.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects single-optimum framing; states contribution push over subsets/segments.

must_hit.point: With ?: mishandling the three letter branches; with a virus string: plain LCS without KMP automaton state; signed imbalance without OFFSET; forgetting parent/redo construction when Checkout/Bookshelf need the actual pack.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names careful ? transitions, LCS+KMP, d+OFFSET, and construction recovery.

probes: What goes wrong if you nest a cnt loop in capacity, skip the freebie/group rewrite, or optimize one pack on a contribution problem?
How do ?, virus-KMP, OFFSET, and parent reconstruction save you on the stretch string/signed/construction items?

hints.1: Check binary grouping, whether a rewrite happened, and contribution vs optimum.
hints.2: Multiples need 1,2,4,…; free-every-k needs sort/freebies or prefix blocks; groups need best[t]; contribution pushes f(sum); ? has three branches; virus needs KMP in LCS; signed needs OFFSET.
hints.3: List: binary-group not cnt; rewrite shop/group story first; contribution not one optimum; careful ? / LCS+KMP; d+OFFSET; parents or redo DP for construction.

tradeoffs.topic: One 0/1 pass vs per-group best[t] then group-knapsack vs contribution over all subsets/segments
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Rewrite the shop/deadline/group story into either (a) one 0/1 pass, (b) per-group best[t] then group-knapsack, or (c) contribution over all subsets/segments—do not force a single optimum when every subset/segment adds f(sum).

tradeoffs.topic: Binary-grouped multiples vs naive cnt loop
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Binary-split counts into 1,2,4,…,remain pseudo-items and run ordinary 0/1; never for _ in cnt inside the capacity loop unless cnt is tiny.

tradeoffs.topic: Full-capacity DP vs weight-class DP vs MITM
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When W is 10^9 but few weight classes (e.g. w_i ∈ [w1, w1+3]), DP on classes/(count, extra-weight); when n≤40 and T is huge, split halves, enumerate 2^{n/2} subset sums, binary-search complements.

tradeoffs.topic: One optimum pack vs contribution DP
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Contribution problems (All Subsets / All Segments) add f(sum) for every subset/segment via push updates (often mod a prime such as 998244353), not a single optimal packing.

tradeoffs.topic: Plain LCS vs LCS + KMP virus automaton
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Lucky Common Subsequence folds a KMP failure link into the LCS state so the forbidden virus string never completes—plain LCS length/alignment is not enough.

When only reachability or uniqueness of a sum matters (Coin Troubles, Unbearable Lightness), use bitset dp |= dp<<w then peel forced items or argue unique totals; keep full DP when values, ways, or reconstruction are needed.

gotchas.trap: Looping cnt naively inside the capacity loop for multiple knapsack.
gotchas.correction: Binary-split counts into 1,2,4,…,remain pseudo-items and run ordinary 0/1 unless cnt is tiny.

gotchas.trap: Coding free-every-k or nested shelves/days as a plain item list without rewriting.
gotchas.correction: Free-every-k: sort ascending, take freebies from the expensive end (hard: prefix sums + paid-block DP). Nested: per-group best[t], then 0/1-knapsack groups into the global budget.

gotchas.trap: Returning one optimal knapsack answer on All Subsets / All Segments.
gotchas.correction: Push contribution updates that add f(sum) for newly formed subset/segment sums (All Subsets often mod 998244353).

gotchas.trap: Full-capacity DP when W is 10^9 or n≤40 with huge T.
gotchas.correction: Few weight classes → DP by class/(count, extra-weight); n≤40 → MITM with sorted 2^{n/2} half sums and complement search.

gotchas.trap: Mishandling ? transitions or ignoring the virus automaton on constrained subsequence/LCS.
gotchas.correction: With ?, multiply/add the three letter branches carefully under mod; with a forbidden pattern, fold KMP failure into the LCS state so the virus never completes.

gotchas.trap: Signed imbalance without OFFSET, or needing the pack but only computing the optimum value.
gotchas.correction: Map difference d to d+OFFSET; recover construction with parent pointers or redo DP knowing the optimum budget (Checkout / Bookshelf).
